examples.solution_text:
(a) Opposite sides give $\overrightarrow{BC}=\overrightarrow{AD}$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AC}&=\overrightarrow{AB}+\overrightarrow{BC}\\&=3\underset{\sim}{u}+2\underset{\sim}{v}\end{aligned}$
(b) Travel from $D$ through $A$ to $B$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{DB}&=\overrightarrow{DA}+\overrightarrow{AB}\\&=-2\underset{\sim}{v}+3\underset{\sim}{u}\\&=3\underset{\sim}{u}-2\underset{\sim}{v}\end{aligned}$
(c) $AE$ is two of the seven equal parts of $AC$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AE}&=\frac{2}{7}\overrightarrow{AC}\\&=\frac{2}{7}\left(3\underset{\sim}{u}+2\underset{\sim}{v}\right)\\&=\frac{6}{7}\underset{\sim}{u}+\frac{4}{7}\underset{\sim}{v}\end{aligned}$

The route $K\to L\to M\to N$ travels against the arrow on $ML$, so $\overrightarrow{LM}=-3\underset{\sim}{q}$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{KN}&=\overrightarrow{KL}+\overrightarrow{LM}+\overrightarrow{MN}\\&=2\underset{\sim}{p}-3\underset{\sim}{q}+\underset{\sim}{r}\end{aligned}$

(a) $AN$ is three of the five equal parts of $AB$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\\&=\underset{\sim}{y}-\underset{\sim}{x}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AN}&=\frac{3}{5}\overrightarrow{AB}\\&=\frac{3}{5}\left(\underset{\sim}{y}-\underset{\sim}{x}\right)\end{aligned}$
(b) Include the initial step from $O$ to $A$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{ON}&=\overrightarrow{OA}+\overrightarrow{AN}\\&=\underset{\sim}{x}+\frac{3}{5}\left(\underset{\sim}{y}-\underset{\sim}{x}\right)\\&=\frac{2}{5}\underset{\sim}{x}+\frac{3}{5}\underset{\sim}{y}\end{aligned}$

Reverse $\overrightarrow{LK}$ using the negative vector law. Combine successive steps using the triangle law.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}\overrightarrow{JK}-\overrightarrow{LK}+\overrightarrow{LM}\\&=\overrightarrow{JK}+\overrightarrow{KL}+\overrightarrow{LM}\\&=\overrightarrow{JL}+\overrightarrow{LM}\\&=\overrightarrow{JM}\end{aligned}$
This equals the right-hand side.

The midpoints give $\overrightarrow{OM}=3\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{ON}=3\underset{\sim}{b}$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MN}&=\overrightarrow{ON}-\overrightarrow{OM}\\&=3\underset{\sim}{b}-3\underset{\sim}{a}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AB}&=\overrightarrow{OB}-\overrightarrow{OA}\\&=6\underset{\sim}{b}-6\underset{\sim}{a}\\&=2\overrightarrow{MN}\end{aligned}$
The non-zero vectors are scalar multiples, so $MN$ is parallel to $AB$.

First find the whole side $BC$ by travelling through $A$ and $D$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{BC}&=\overrightarrow{BA}+\overrightarrow{AD}+\overrightarrow{DC}\\&=2\underset{\sim}{v}+3\underset{\sim}{w}-\underset{\sim}{u}\end{aligned}$
Since $M$ is the midpoint, the reverse half-step is
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MB}&=-\frac{1}{2}\overrightarrow{BC}\\&=-\underset{\sim}{v}-\frac{3}{2}\underset{\sim}{w}+\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{u}\end{aligned}$
Use the route $M\to B\to A$.
$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MA}&=\overrightarrow{MB}+\overrightarrow{BA}\\&=-\underset{\sim}{v}-\frac{3}{2}\underset{\sim}{w}+\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{u}+2\underset{\sim}{v}\\&=\frac{1}{2}\underset{\sim}{u}+\underset{\sim}{v}-\frac{3}{2}\underset{\sim}{w}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Equal opposite-side vectors give AC=3u+2v. The journey D→A→B gives DB=-2v+3u. AE:EC=2:5 gives AE=(2/7)AC=(6/7)u+(4/7)v. The diagram places E at exactly 2/7 of AC, within coordinate rounding. Supported by the parallelogram example at lines 2530–2540 and internal division at lines 3594–3603.
Along K→L→M→N, KL=2p, LM=-3q and MN=r, so KN=2p-3q+r. All three diagram arrows agree with the givens. This follows the directed quadrilateral journeys at lines 3499–3529.

QR=PR-PQ=3b-2a. Hence QM=(1/2)QR=(3/2)b-a, and PM=PQ+QM=a+(3/2)b. M=(3,1.5) is the midpoint of the authored Q and R coordinates. Both derived solution arrows have the correct endpoints and directions. The method matches lines 3295–3310.

AB=y-x and AN=(3/5)(y-x). Therefore ON=x+AN=(2/5)x+(3/5)y. The authored N coordinates equal A+(3/5)(B-A), confirming AN:NB=3:2. The method matches internal division and the initial journey at lines 3594–3603.

Replacing -LK with KL gives JK+KL+LM. The triangle law reduces this to JL+LM=JM. The given arrows match JK, LK and LM. The bare opening expression has the required phantom relation gutter. This adapts the identities at lines 2622–2641.

OM=3a and ON=3b, so MN=3b-3a. AB=6b-6a=2MN. Since A and B are distinct, AB and MN are non-zero, establishing parallelism. Both marked points are exact midpoints in the diagram. This follows the midpoint parallel proof at lines 3853–3865.

BC=BA+AD+DC=2v+3w-u. Thus MB=-(1/2)BC=-v-(3/2)w+(1/2)u. Adding BA gives MA=(1/2)u+v-(3/2)w. M is the exact midpoint of the authored B and C coordinates; all given arrows have the correct directions. The method matches lines 3951–3975.

Relation gutters are consistent, phantom ink is invisible, and diagram labels, arrows and relationships are readable and correct. The solution-only annotations in example 3 disappear in question-only views. No consequential clipping, overlap or answer leakage was found.
